title: Survival, Fossils, and Change
intro: Sort fossil clues, how well organisms fit a place, and what animal groups give and cost.
note: This is a sorting game model, and the real habitat-change claim, comparing a solution's benefits and costs, still counts.
summary: Fossils such as Michigan Petoskey stones show past organisms and environments, and a habitat fits some organisms well but not others. Groups can help animals survive, but they also bring trade-offs, and a winter model showed 8 thick-fur deer surviving compared with 2 thin-fur deer.

stages.prompt: What past environment does this fossil evidence support?

cards.label: Petoskey stone
cards.why: A Petoskey stone is fossil coral. Coral needs shallow water, so this shows an ancient sea in Michigan.
cards.hint: What kind of place does coral need?

cards.label: Fossil coral
cards.why: Coral needs shallow water, so the place was once a warm shallow sea.
cards.hint: What kind of place does coral need?

cards.label: Fern leaf fossil
cards.why: A fern leaf fossil points to wet land.
cards.hint: What kind of place does a fern need?

cards.label: Fish fossil
cards.why: A fish needed water, but this fossil does not tell us if it was a lake or a sea.
cards.hint: what does a fish need, and does the fossil say more?

stages.prompt: How well does this organism survive in this place?

cards.label: Frog in a pond
cards.why: A frog survives well in a pond because it needs water.
cards.hint: does this place give the animal what it needs?

cards.label: Deer in a forest
cards.why: A deer survives well in a forest because it finds food and cover.
cards.hint: What can a deer find in this place?

cards.label: Beach grass on a dune
cards.hint: Does this plant fit this kind of place?

cards.label: Fish on dry land
cards.why: A fish cannot survive on land because its gills only work in water.
cards.hint: What do gills need in order to work?

cards.label: Deer on a bare sand dune
cards.why: A bare dune has little of the food and cover a deer needs, so it survives less well there than in a forest.
cards.hint: how much of the food and cover it needs does this place give?

cards.label: Beach grass in a shady forest
cards.why: Beach grass fits sunny, sandy dunes. In a shady forest it gets less of what it needs, so it survives less well.
cards.hint: does this place give the plant the light and sand it fits?

stages.prompt: Does this show a way the group helps, or a trade-off?

cards.label: Wolves hunting in a pack
cards.why: Wolves hunt in packs, which can help them get food.
cards.hint: could several wolves together catch food that one wolf could not?

cards.label: Bees sharing the work
cards.why: Bees share work, which can help the group survive.
cards.hint: what gets done faster when many bees each do a job?

cards.label: Many deer watching
cards.why: Many eyes can see danger sooner than one deer alone.
cards.hint: what can many deer see that one deer might miss?

cards.label: Sharing limited food
cards.why: Groups may have to share food, so there is less for each animal.
cards.hint: what happens to each animal's share when more animals eat the same food?

cards.label: Crowding in limited space
cards.why: When many animals live close together they crowd each other, and that can make fighting and sickness spread more easily. That is a cost of living in a group.
cards.hint: what happens when many animals need the same small space?
